title: Improving without hiding failures
goals: Check that earlier behavior still works
Keep a truthful change and failure record

prerequisite.prompt: Why rerun old passing cases after a fix?
prerequisite.answer: The change may introduce a regression elsewhere.

vocabulary: Earlier cases rerun after a change
A record of what changed and why
The underlying reason for a failure
A limitation or possible failure remaining after a repair

blocks.text: A fictional chooser wrongly excludes an activity at the exact time limit because it uses minutes < limit. The requirement says at most, so equality must qualify. Repair that condition, then test below, at and above the boundary plus earlier tie and invalid-input behavior.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: The repaired predicate prints 9 True, 10 True and 11 False. It assumes validated numeric durations; it is not a replacement for the schema validator. A focused change is easier to explain and evaluate than unrelated edits made at the same time.

blocks.label: Would changing the condition to minutes <= limit + 1 correctly repair the boundary? Explain with a revealing input.

blocks.text: Changing the expected boundary result to False would make the test pass while violating the requirement. Keep the requirement and independently calculated expectation; repair the implementation. If requirements truly change, document that as a policy change.

A clean regression run does not erase the earlier failure. Keep before/after evidence and remaining limitations. If a fix was informed by reserved evaluation cases, report that contamination and obtain new independent cases.

blocks.label: Record the bug, change, evidence and one remaining limit without claiming all bugs are gone.

workbook.title: Locate the cause
workbook.prompt: Why does minutes < limit reject a valid exactly-at-limit activity?
workbook.answer: Strict less-than excludes equality; at most requires <=.

workbook.title: Test neighbors
workbook.prompt: For limit 15, give expected eligibility at 14, 15 and 16.

workbook.title: Reject a bad fix
workbook.prompt: A proposed fix accepts minutes <= limit + 1. Give a counterexample at limit 15.
workbook.answer: It accepts 16, which should be excluded.

workbook.title: Repair independently
workbook.prompt: Write the eligibility predicate for at most 12 minutes and a regression set including 11,12,13 and 0. Add one chooser tie case and one invalid-data case to rerun.
workbook.answer: Use minutes <= limit after validation. Expectations True, True, False, True. Include a deterministic tie case and a schema-invalid row that never reaches selection; state expected outcomes.

workbook.title: Write the change log
workbook.prompt: Record the bug, change, evidence and one remaining limit without claiming all bugs are gone.
workbook.answer: The strict comparison excluded the boundary; changed < to <=; below/at/above and prior checks rerun; finite tests and untested situations remain. Accept equivalent specific records.

teacher.background: Teach Week 35 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. A fictional chooser wrongly excludes an activity at the exact time limit because it uses minutes < limit. The requirement says at most, so equality must qualify. Repair that condition, then test below, at and above the boundary plus earlier tie and invalid-input behavior. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.
materials: Python 3 editor with a fresh local practice file
Paper trace table and the student workbook
Fictional input records from this lesson; no real student identifiers
sessions: Retrieve the prerequisite and explain the purpose in the opening section.
Read the worked example and diagram; ask learners to trace each step aloud.
Complete W1 and W2, then compare predictions with observed results.
Collect the guided prediction before running; discuss a mismatch and its cause.
Retrieve the main rule without showing the previous answer.
Use W3 to diagnose and repair the stated failure; rerun an earlier case.
Collect W4 independently, including code or plan, predictions and explanations, before hints.
Discuss W5 and the exit; use the fresh retry when support was needed.
